Although I usually prefer using my iPhone naked — without a case or screen protector — this time with the iPhone 17 Pro I'm using both, and I can recommend them to everyone. Neither accessory is expensive, so even if you buy them just to try, you're not losing out; if you find they don't suit you after trying, you can simply not keep them on long-term.

Five years ago, Apple introduced Ceramic Shield glass to the iPhone screen, claiming a fourfold improvement in drop test performance and promising that iPhone screens would be much less prone to shattering.

My iPhone screen has never cracked to this day, but after about a year of use, two or three fairly deep scratches always appear on the screen.

This year's Ceramic Shield 2 front glass is claimed to offer three times better scratch resistance.

Apple also says the anti-reflective performance of this front glass has improved, but compared with the nano-texture anti-glare treatment on the iPad Pro and MacBook Pro, the gap is still obvious.

Add a more matte texture to your iPhone 17 Pro screen

For these reasons, I've gone back to using a product I tried a few years ago and found quite good — namely Mothca's matte glass screen protector.

This product isn't perfect. If there were an iPhone with nano-texture but without that slight rainbow effect and reduction in brightness, I'd be even happier.

However, if you like the look of a matte screen, I still recommend giving it a try — especially since a single pack or double pack is only US$9 and US$14 respectively, and the feel is far more premium than the price suggests.

A slim case suited for "just in case"

When it comes to iPhone cases, I don't want to spend too much, because I don't plan to use one every day.

I usually only put on a case before activities like kayaking, or mounting the iPhone on a motorcycle handlebar. I'm also worried that the sharp corners of the camera bump will scratch that orange aluminium frame.

I like black, but I felt that black paired with the everyday Cosmic Orange had a slight Halloween vibe. So I decided to pick a greyer colour to go with the orange, creating a kind of futuristic spacesuit look.

I bought this case on a whim at the store a few days ago and found I was very happy with it.

This is the Spigen Thin Fit case, available in black, gunmetal grey and deep sea green. I chose the grey, which felt just right for the look I was after.

Spigen's retail price is US$39.99, but the same one sells for US$34.99 on Amazon.

I've noticed that many cheap cases don't have built-in MagSafe, which affects the performance of external batteries and magnetic stands.

The Spigen Thin Fit has built-in MagSafe, and the Camera Control area uses a capacitive cover design rather than just a cut-out.

I like that this case completely wraps around the entire camera "plateau", because the durability of that area is what I'm most concerned about.

Once fitted, it also creates a rather stylish "orange ring" look, reminiscent of the Digital Crown on the Space Black Apple Watch Ultra.

Apart from the cut-out at the bottom, the Cosmic Orange colour also shows through the edges of the button covers, achieving the grey-with-orange-accents effect I wanted.

Another benefit is that with the case on, you can't see the orange aluminium frame around the screen. It looks fine when the case is off, but paired with a black case, it becomes just a thin orange line separating the black case from the black screen, which I find very jarring.

Two budget iPhone 17 Pro accessory recommendations

The Mothca screen protector can help you avoid deep scratches, and if you like an anti-glare screen, that matte feel is also excellent. The Spigen Thin Fit case has a metallic feel, is smooth to the touch, and won't make the phone too bulky.

Make the most of your Apple products
